title: orch Needs you v1 (stdout of `orch needs --json`)
description: What waits for a person, one list for every surface (terminal, browser, phone). The core makes its rows from tickets alone: open questions and waits past their `until`. An active add-on whose manifest has `needs = true` adds rows through `orch <name> needs --json` (same row shape, pulled with a 2 s timeout; on failure its last rows come back with stale = true). Rows are sorted questions first, then bad, then warn; ids are stable and unique, so a surface can remember what it showed. Unknown fields are kept.

id.description: <source>:<stable key>. Core: core:q:<ticket id>:<question id> and core:wait:<ticket id>.

source.description: core, or the add-on name that made the row.

kind.description: question (a plain open question), overdue-wait (waiting_on.until passed, any wait kind), or <add-on>:<name> (a question of that kind, or an add-on's own row).

title.description: Plain text (shown with textContent): usually the ticket title.

text.description: Plain text: the question, or what is late.

since.description: Since when it waits (question asked, wait passed, event time).

answer.description: Present when the row can be answered in place: `orch answer <ticket> <question> <option>`.

cli.description: Optional command that settles the row, shown to people who use the terminal.

actions.description: Optional buttons of an add-on's own row (a page shows them instead of the answer options). Each runs `orch <source> act <verb> -- <target>` through the one generic add-on op; `sign` = the person's sign step first (the page asks the add-on `act <verb> --proof-target` for the target and the review it shows, and mints only that target, only ever `addon.act` under the add-on's own name). `later` hides the row for a day, `view` opens a ticket's file, `op` may only name a core op the page already signs (private.move, only in rows from the add-on that owns it; its label and review are the page's own).

review.description: Row wording (title, body, here, there, done; plain text). The sign step shows the add-on's --proof-target review instead; only `done` words the toast.

stale.description: true = an add-on's row from its last good pull (the pull failed or timed out now).
